While you were at the Pool of Tears, one of Fel'zerul's scouts brought back a scroll inked in blood on dried flesh. Fel'zerul now bundles the artifacts you gathered and sends you far north to the Hinterlands, to find an exiled Atal'ai priest.

The scroll reads as a judicial ruling against a priest of the Atal'ai, a fate worse than death among his own people. He was exiled to live among the Witherbark trolls, far to the north in the Hinterlands. Fel'zerul will bundle the artifacts and sends you to find the exile, discover their true use, and return.

Messenger to Westfall is an Alliance errand carrying an urgent plea from Magistrate Solomon in Redridge across Elwynn to Westfall. Facing total abandonment by the Stormwind military, Lakeshire's leadership seeks mutual aid from Gryan Stoutmantle's newly formed People's Militia.

Magistrate Solomon finds Lakeshire in a desperate situation. The Redridge Mountains are besieged by Blackrock orcs and gnolls, yet the Stormwind Army has failed to arrive in force. Recognizing that Lakeshire cannot survive on town guards and irregulars alone, Solomon writes a formal plea for assistance. With regular royal reserves nowhere in sight, he turns his eyes west, having heard word of a citizen defense group forming beyond Elwynn Forest.

The intended recipient of the dispatch is Gryan Stoutmantle, a veteran commander who has begun rallying volunteer fighters under the banner of the People's Militia. By sending a courier directly across the kingdom, Solomon hopes that Westfall's organized volunteers might spare troops to reinforce Lakeshire's borders until the Crown's armies finally mobilize. However, as messengers soon discover, Westfall is mired in its own catastrophic struggles against the Defias Brotherhood.
Why is Magistrate Solomon asking Westfall for help?

Stormwind has failed to send the military reinforcements Lakeshire urgently needs against the orcs and gnolls. Having heard reports of an armed citizen force gathering in Westfall, Solomon hopes Gryan Stoutmantle can spare troops to reinforce Redridge.

Dar promises to make a trip to the coast worth your while if you bring back some of their legs, to be sent on to Orgrimmar. Dar is pleased with the legs, imagining them perfectly cooked over an open fire. Dar urges you to take a cooked sample along on your travels and swears it is truly delicious.

Thrall seeks a careful hand to preserve peace with the Alliance. In Orgrimmar, Craven Drok sends seasoned Horde adventurers to find Keldran near the western exit. The work calls for quiet diplomacy and intelligence to protect Thrall’s fragile peace.

Thrall knows war with the Alliance could ruin his young nation. Raised in human captivity, the Warchief learned human statecraft and military strategy. Craven Drok watches for warriors and champions with patience for a subtler path, one that looks beyond raw force.

Near Orgrimmar’s western exit, Keldran keeps a humble dwelling. He practices magic and covert arts, working with appearances, perception, and statecraft. Keldran seeks discreet operatives to serve the Warchief as the Horde faces a tense standoff with its bitter rivals.

In Orgrimmar, Alliance advances across Kalimdor raise fears of dangerous political fallout. The Horde sends orders to Desolace to purge demons before the Alliance can accuse Thrall's people of renewed ties to the Burning Legion.

Alliance scouts and expeditions crossing Kalimdor put the Horde in a delicate position. Demonic remnants across central Kalimdor could confirm old suspicions that the orcs and their allies still serve the Burning Legion. With Warchief Thrall's sanction, Keldran oversees operations from Orgrimmar to clear those remnants before hostile Alliance factions can use them to justify war.

Orders south lead through the Charred Vale in the Stonetalon Mountains and into Desolace. Just north of the vast Kodo Graveyard stands Ghost Walker Post. Horde agents such as Takata Steelblade watch the wastes, where rampant centaur tribes and spreading demonic corruption both threaten the region.

Takata Steelblade sees the assignment with grim pragmatism. Clearing the local demons also eases pressure on violent centaur tribes and helps the Horde's resident warlocks. Still, the duty comes first: removing the Burning Legion's footholds protects the Horde, whatever others gain from the purge.
Why is the Horde concerned about the Alliance here?

Alliance forces advancing across Kalimdor could use active demon infestations as proof that the Horde still consorts with the Burning Legion. By purging local demons, the Horde hopes to blunt those accusations.

Dalinda Malem tells you the orcs slaughtered all their guards and servants before bringing her and Tyranis here. Tyranis tried to speak to them, and she cannot leave until she knows what has become of her brother. She asks you to find him and come back when his fate is known.

She will not escape until she knows his fate, so she asks you to find him and return when you do. He is in a building left of the fortress entrance.

Dalinda dreads that Tyranis, if allowed, will seek the Burning Blade's secrets and become one of them. Power has always drawn him, as it does anyone magic seduces. To her people even studying such things is a grave crime, and she doubts she could face her family with word that his spirit toyed with that danger.

When you come back, Dalinda calls it terrible but necessary. If your hand had not done it, her own people's would have. She asks pardon if her thanks sounds hollow. Knowing his fate, she is ready to escape and will accept your help if you are still willing.

A letter from Westfall brings Magistrate Solomon a hard answer in Lakeshire. He asked Gryan Stoutmantle for soldiers to defend Redridge, but Westfall has been left to face its own troubles.

Magistrate Solomon faces growing troubles in the Redridge Mountains without Stormwind's royal garrison. He looks to the southern frontier for help and writes to Gryan Stoutmantle, commander of the People's Militia in Westfall. Solomon hopes the volunteers at Sentinel Hill can spare fighters to strengthen Lakeshire's defenses. He does not know how hard pressed the western plains are.

Gryan Stoutmantle refuses, though the answer weighs heavily on him. Westfall is fighting the Defias Brotherhood and marauding gnolls because the House of Nobles and the crown have abandoned the kingdom's breadbasket. The People's Militia formed so the people could survive. Its ranks lose good men each day, and Stoutmantle cannot spare a single fighter for Redridge.

When you carry Stoutmantle's reply back to Lakeshire, Solomon sees that the frontier territories share the same neglect. Local magistrates and citizen militias are left to defend themselves while the Stormwind Army remains withheld. Solomon turns his attention south, toward Darkshire in Duskwood, hoping to find aid there.

Magistrate Solomon sought help because Lakeshire faces growing threats without Stormwind's army. He knew Gryan Stoutmantle had organized the People's Militia to defend Westfall and hoped it could spare soldiers for Redridge.

You cross the sea to Darkshore in search of a Kor gem for Jordan Stilwell. Thundris Windweaver sends an Alliance paladin initiate into Blackfathom Deeps, where naga corrupt the potent stone. Jordan needs it for his craft.

Paladins in training cross continental borders to Darkshore for materials needed by the human smith Jordan Stilwell. In Auberdine, the night elf Thundris Windweaver remembers the blacksmith with respect. Night elves keep their distance, and some fallen humans have betrayed their trust, yet Thundris still believes paladins can follow a righteous path. He tells them where ancient gems can be found.

Blackfathom Deeps lies beneath the foggy northwestern coast of Ashenvale. Twilight's Hammer cultists and treacherous sea-dwellers inhabit its submerged halls. Naga priestesses there channel foul magic through ancient Kor gems. The gem you seek is deep within the temple complex, amid its dark halls and dangerous inhabitants.

When you return a corrupted Kor gem to Thundris Windweaver, he must remove the darkness before Jordan Stilwell can forge it into a holy weapon. The naga give the gem raw magical potency, but twist its enchantment toward evil. Thundris cleanses that corruption so the gem's power stays pure and stable for the sacred smithing ritual ahead.
